toegepas.blok: Stysel in die kos wat ons eet
toegepas.voor: 'n Gekookte eier en 'n stukkie gewone blokkaas bly dus bruin in die jodiumtoets.
toegepas.na: Op 'n gekookte eier en 'n stukkie gewone blokkaas bly die jodiumoplossing dus bruin.
toegepas.rede_vinder: As written the egg and cheese themselves 'stay brown', but it is the iodine solution that stays brown on them; the protected 'gewone blokkaas' is kept.
toegepas.fout: The sentence says the egg and the cheese themselves stay brown, but it is the iodine solution on them that stays brown.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The proposal says what actually stays brown, keeps 'gewone blokkaas' and 'dus', mirrors the aartappel sentence before it, and does not change the claim.

laat_vaar.na: dié in die suikerpot by die huis
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The lesson addresses the learner as 'jy' throughout, so the sudden plural 'julle' is inconsistent; this keeps the household meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'julle suikerpot' is natural Afrikaans for the household's sugar pot even when one child is addressed, so this is a lateral move, and 'dié in die suikerpot' stacks two near-identical words.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: uit sy kos, en ook 'n dier wat die plant eet
laat_vaar_vorige.na: uit sy kos, en 'n dier wat die plant eet, kry dit ook
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The tacked-on phrase without its own verb reads awkwardly; giving it a verb makes a proper second clause that justifies the comma.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The elliptical 'en ook 'n dier wat die plant eet' is acceptable Afrikaans, while the proposal is longer and its 'dit' could point to either 'energie' or 'kos'.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Stysel in die kos wat ons eet
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: kan wel stysel bevat as mense dit bygevoeg het
laat_vaar_vorige.na: kan wel stysel bevat wat mense bygevoeg het
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'dit' can be read as the sausage rather than the starch; a relative clause makes clear it is the starch that was added.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'dit' naturally points to the starch, and swapping conditional 'as' for relative 'wat' drops the condition that starch is there only if people added it.
